claims.text: As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The reported 13.5% terminal strain is a baseline tensile elongation or tensile-ductility value for HfZrTiTa0.53.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has high impact-triggered chemical-energy release.
Cold rolling increases dislocation density in the treated alloy.
Annealing after cold rolling promotes recrystallization and can generate finer grains.
A 40% cold reduction followed by annealing at 700°C for 10 minutes will produce a refined, uniform equiaxed grain structure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed sequential cold-rolling and annealing treatment generates the mediator through partial dynamic recrystallization.
The refined, uniform grain structure activates additional slip systems.
The refined structure and controlled dislocation density delay strain localization.
The proposed treatment will increase uniform tensile elongation from 13.5% to approximately 20% at room temperature and about 10^-3 s^-1.
The treated alloy's yield strength will remain within 10% of the as-cast baseline.
The treated alloy's compressive strength will remain within 10% of the as-cast baseline.
The treated alloy's impact-triggered energy release will remain comparable to the as-cast value.
Excessive annealing can coarsen recrystallized grains and reduce strength.
The treatment is expected to remain effective during unspecified high-strain-rate impact loading.

contradictions.description: The query attributes enhanced chemical-energy release to WFeNiMo fragments, whereas the hypothesis treats high impact-triggered energy release as an established baseline property of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The query reports 13.5% as the terminal strain alongside compressive properties, but the hypothesis repeatedly reclassifies it as tensile elongation or uniform tensile strain.

The intervention specifies deformation followed by a separate anneal, which ordinarily invokes static recrystallization, while the structural mediator calls the process partial dynamic recrystallization.
